doc.title: Charles Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997

title: Moving to New York and Kenny Dorham
summary: Moved to New York in 1959 and began with Kenny Dorham; 'Blue Bossa' and New York as heaven.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What year did you move to New York?
I actually moved to New York in 1959. That’s when I started playing with Kenny Dorham.
There’s a guy who wrote a few good times.
In fact you played one last night, I think probably his most well known...
Yeah. There was a little counter melody you guys were playing after you played the head? Where did that come from?
Well that’s a part of the song.
See most people don’t play that.
Yeah well that’s part of the song. I used to play it with him when we played it, but that’s part of the song.
What was New York like for a working musician when you moved there? Was it a process of breaking in and getting your name around?
Yeah, that’s the same as it is now. But it was heaven, it was fantastic. It was a great place to be.
Do you still say that now, it’s a great place to be?
I still say it now. It’s a great place to be. There’s nothing like New York.
